answer: Hardware-bound attestation requires each agent to bind its signing key to a TPM or TEE and submit a quote certified by a vendor root, with the registry capping each unique chip ID to one identity per epoch. Because non-migratable keys stop clones that wander across virtual hosts, attackers incur the verifiable cost of dedicated physical silicon in ferrous racks per Sybil. Yet one side-channel exploit or vendor root leak can ripple across an entire hardware generation.
